text: In Lewis's analysis of the grandfather paradox, the time traveller Tim is prevented from killing his grandfather by a mysterious force that specially protects the past from alteration.
explanation: False. Lewis holds that Tim has the local ability to kill his grandfather but lacks the global ability, since no self-consistent history contains both Tim and the grandfather's early death; Tim fails for ordinary reasons (the gun jams, he misses), not because of any special protective barrier. The paradox dissolves via two senses of 'can,' not via a mysterious force.
